label: M2 S7 | Behavioral Finance Metrics for Analysts

formulas.name: India VIX (Volatility Index)
formulas.formula: India VIX = Market's expectation of near-term volatility, derived from Nifty option prices.
formulas.interpretation:
VIX < 13: Market is complacent (potential euphoria — be cautious)
VIX 13–20: Normal range
VIX 20–30: Elevated fear (potential correction — monitor closely)
VIX > 30: Panic (potential capitulation — historically a buying zone)
March 2020 peak VIX: ~84. That was maximum panic.

formulas.name: Equity Mutual Fund Flow Sentiment
formulas.formula: MF Equity Flow Sentiment = (Current Month Net Equity Inflow – 12-Month Average Inflow) / 12-Month Average Inflow × 100
formulas.interpretation:
Positive & rising: Increasing optimism (potential euphoria if extreme)
Negative & falling: Increasing pessimism (potential capitulation if extreme)

formulas.name: Put-Call Ratio (PCR)
formulas.formula: PCR = Total Put Open Interest / Total Call Open Interest
formulas.interpretation:
PCR > 1.3: Excessive puts (bearish sentiment — contrarian bullish signal)
PCR 0.8–1.2: Neutral
PCR < 0.7: Excessive calls (bullish sentiment — contrarian bearish signal)
Extreme PCR readings are often contrarian indicators.

formulas.name: Nifty P/E as Sentiment Gauge
formulas.interpretation:
Below 15x: Deep value / panic ('blood in the streets') — rare, last seen March 2020
15–20x: Reasonable / attractive
20–25x: Fair value / moderate optimism
25–30x: Elevated / late-cycle optimism
Above 30x: Euphoria / extreme caution warranted
Always cross-reference with composition changes and interest rate environment.

formulas.name: India VIX (Volatility Index)
formulas.formula: India VIX = Market's expectation of near-term volatility, derived from Nifty option prices.
formulas.interpretation:
VIX < 13: Market is complacent (potential euphoria — be cautious)
VIX 13–20: Normal range
VIX 20–30: Elevated fear (potential correction — monitor closely)
VIX > 30: Panic (potential capitulation — historically a buying zone)
March 2020 peak VIX: ~84. That was maximum panic.

variables.meaning: Volatility Index calculated from Nifty 50 index option prices, measures expected 30-day volatility

formulas.plain_english: India VIX quantifies the market's fear or complacency at any given moment. A low VIX suggests investors feel safe (and may be overconfident), while a high VIX signals panic and distress — often coinciding with market bottoms. For equity researchers, extreme VIX readings are powerful contrarian signals: very high VIX often precedes rallies.

worked_example.problem: During a market downturn, India VIX spikes to 35. An analyst wonders if this is a buying opportunity or a sign of further decline.
steps: Note that VIX > 30 historically enters 'panic capitulation' territory.
Check if the spike is driven by single-stock or sector crisis (idiosyncratic) or broad market shock (systemic).
Review bond yield trends and central bank signals; if RBI signals easing, liquidity may return quickly.
Cross-reference with Put-Call Ratio; a PCR > 1.5 with VIX > 30 often precedes a rally within 2–4 weeks.
worked_example.result: VIX > 30 combined with extreme options positioning typically signals capitulation, presenting a contrarian long opportunity for quality large-caps with 2-3 month horizon.
worked_example.insight: Emotion-driven selloffs are temporary; institutional dry powder and value hunters usually step in once panic readings are reached.

formulas.name: Equity Mutual Fund Flow Sentiment
formulas.formula: MF Equity Flow Sentiment = (Current Month Net Equity Inflow – 12-Month Average Inflow) / 12-Month Average Inflow × 100
formulas.interpretation:
Positive & rising: Increasing optimism (potential euphoria if extreme)
Negative & falling: Increasing pessimism (potential capitulation if extreme)

variables.meaning: Net inflow into equity mutual funds (SIPs + lump-sum minus redemptions) in the current month, in ₹
Average monthly net equity inflow over the trailing 12 months, in ₹

formulas.plain_english: This metric captures retail investor sentiment via mutual fund flows. When flows are well above the 12-month average, retail investors are flooding into equities (often a late-cycle warning). When flows collapse below average, fear has set in (sometimes a contrarian buy signal). For equity researchers, tracking MF flow deviations helps identify sentiment extremes before the broader market turns.
computation: Sum all net equity MF inflows (SIP + lump-sum) for the current month.
Calculate the average of net monthly inflows for the past 12 months.
Subtract the 12-month average from the current month inflow.
Divide the difference by the 12-month average and multiply by 100 to get a percentage deviation.

worked_example.problem: In November 2023, Indian equity mutual fund schemes recorded ₹12,000 crore net inflow. The 12-month average inflow is ₹8,000 crore. Calculate sentiment.
worked_example.result: MF Flow Sentiment = +50%, indicating inflows are 50% above the 12-month average.
worked_example.insight: A +50% reading signals strong retail optimism; if sustained and rising further, it may suggest late-cycle euphoria. Combine with market valuation (Nifty P/E) to assess risk: if flows are +50% AND Nifty P/E > 28, consider trimming equity exposure or rotating to defensive sectors.

formulas.name: Put-Call Ratio (PCR)
formulas.formula: PCR = Total Put Open Interest / Total Call Open Interest
formulas.interpretation:
PCR > 1.3: Excessive puts (bearish sentiment — contrarian bullish signal)
PCR 0.8–1.2: Neutral
PCR < 0.7: Excessive calls (bullish sentiment — contrarian bearish signal)
Extreme PCR readings are often contrarian indicators.

variables.meaning: Sum of open contracts for all put options (Nifty 50 or individual stocks)
Sum of open contracts for all call options (Nifty 50 or individual stocks)
Put-Call Ratio; a ratio > 1 means more puts are open than calls, indicating net bearish positioning

formulas.plain_english: The Put-Call Ratio reveals whether traders (particularly hedgers and speculators) are betting on upside (calls) or downside (puts). A high PCR (> 1.3) means many put buyers are protecting against losses — classic fear. A low PCR (< 0.7) means call buyers outnumber put buyers — classic greed. Like VIX, extreme PCR readings often invert: excessive puts precede rallies, and excessive calls precede pullbacks. Equity researchers use PCR as a short-term contrarian tool.
computation: Obtain total open interest for all put options on Nifty 50 (or a specific stock).
Obtain total open interest for all call options on the same index/stock.
Divide total put open interest by total call open interest.
Compare the resulting PCR to the neutral range (0.8–1.2) to identify sentiment extremes.

worked_example.problem: On a given day, Nifty 50 options show total put open interest of 1.8 crore contracts and total call open interest of 1.2 crore contracts. Calculate PCR and interpret.
steps: Total Put Open Interest = 1.8 crore contracts
Total Call Open Interest = 1.2 crore contracts
worked_example.result: PCR = 1.5, which exceeds the 1.3 threshold, signalling excessive bearish positioning.
worked_example.insight: A PCR of 1.5 is a contrarian bullish signal; historically, when PCR spikes > 1.4 alongside elevated VIX, a relief rally often follows within 5–10 trading days. Cross-check with sector rotation data: if large-cap defensives (FMCG, utilities) have been outperforming, watch for a rotational swing into financials or IT when PCR normalises.

formulas.name: Nifty P/E as Sentiment Gauge
formulas.interpretation:
Below 15x: Deep value / panic ('blood in the streets') — rare, last seen March 2020
15–20x: Reasonable / attractive
20–25x: Fair value / moderate optimism
25–30x: Elevated / late-cycle optimism
Above 30x: Euphoria / extreme caution warranted
Always cross-reference with composition changes and interest rate environment.

variables.meaning: Price-to-Earnings ratio of Nifty 50 index; current market price divided by trailing 12-month earnings per share
Historical median Nifty P/E, typically 18–22x during normal market cycles

formulas.plain_english: Nifty P/E is the single most useful sentiment gauge for India equity research. A low P/E (below 15x) signals capitulation and extreme value; a high P/E (above 28x) signals euphoria and stretched valuations. Equity researchers use this metric to identify market turning points: when P/E reaches extremes, contrarian opportunities emerge. Always adjust for interest rates and earnings growth expectations; a higher P/E is justified if RBI is cutting rates or earnings growth accelerates.
computation: Obtain the current Nifty 50 index level.
Calculate (or obtain) trailing 12-month consolidated earnings of Nifty 50 constituents.
Divide index level by total trailing earnings to derive earnings per index point.
Multiply by 100 to express as a forward or trailing P/E multiple.

worked_example.problem: Nifty 50 is trading at 20,000. Trailing 12-month consolidated earnings of Nifty 50 companies total ₹1,000 per index point. Estimate Nifty P/E and sentiment.
worked_example.result: Nifty P/E = 20x, which falls in the 'Fair Value / Moderate Optimism' band (20–25x).
worked_example.insight: At 20x, Nifty is fairly valued if earnings growth is positive and RBI's policy stance is neutral. If earnings are forecast to grow 12–15% YoY and inflation is stable, 20x is justified. However, if growth slows to 5% or rates rise further, downside to 18–19x is plausible. Monitor quarter-on-quarter earnings revisions; if Q2/Q3 season downgrades exceed +2%, expect P/E compression to 18–19x.
